unit.why: A single narrative: the tsaddik of Rozdol shuts himself in with his dying daughter Hinda, means to revive her as Elisha did, is stopped by his late father-in-law, and later recounts all this in the sukkah.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי מאיש ת"ח וחסיד עובד ה׳
stories.end_quote: כאור נוגה אור ח׳ וכו׳ עכד״ק
stories.summary_en: When his daughter Hinda lay dying, the tsaddik of Rozdol shut himself in alone with her, meaning to revive her as Elisha revived the Shunammite's son, because he grieved for the broken bond with the Sasov dynasty; his father-in-law came and warned him off as dangerous, and on Sukkot night he told the story at the meal and then gave a Torah teaching.
